description: Switches Developer options' "Don't keep activities" (always_finish_activities) the way Settings does, so it takes effect at once: with it on, Android destroys every activity as soon as it is no longer visible (HOME, or opening the next screen), and the app must restore it from its saved state when the user comes back. A plain `settings put` changes only the stored value, which the system reads at boot. verified: the activity manager reports the new state (`dumpsys activity processes`) and, when turning it on, activities that were in the background with their process were destroyed (destroyCheck; null when there were none to watch or it was on already). verified: false with destroyCheck.destroyed 0 means "not destroyed yet": Android does it at its next process-priority update. If it cannot be switched on, the call fails and nothing is changed. What Lionscope turned on it puts back as it was when the device's profiling session stops or Lionscope stops, and retries a failed put-back when the device reconnects (autoOff; status shows it per device). enabled: false on a device Lionscope switched on puts it back as it was. Use get_activity_instance before and after to see an activity recreated. A global developer setting for every app on the device: tell the user you turned it on, and turn it off (enabled: false) when you are done. Device control.

enabled.description: true: destroy activities when they leave the screen; false: back to normal.

serial.description: adb serial; default: the session device, or the only ready one.

name: set_dont_keep_activities
title: Don't keep activities
